name: Bilzen, c. 1650
attribution: Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); historical land cover, town walls and gates from the Ferraris map (1777) and the Villaret map (1745-48), Digitaal Vlaanderen (geo.api.vlaanderen.be/HISTCART)

walls.source: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Bilzen' (https://id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140045)
walls.note: Bilzen wall with gates on its main roads (rebuilt 1506; plundered 1636 by Jan van Weert, 1654 by Lorraine troops; partly razed by the French 1675). Traced from the Ferraris map (1777).

landmarks.y1650: Parish church (main bell tower), plundered 1576; rebuilt after the fire of 1636.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Bilzen' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140045)

landmarks.y1650: Beguinage founded 1256 in the south-east of the town, with a hospital.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Bilzen' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140045)

ruler.name: Prinsbisdom Luik
ruler.sovereign: Prince-bishop Ferdinand of Bavaria (1612-50), then Maximilian Henry of Bavaria (elected 1650); neutral in the Franco-Spanish war (neutrality recognised by Spain only in 1654, see history-check F76)

overworld.note: coordinates are overworld metres: town-local metres (around origin) + centre; 1:1 scale inside radius
